text:
Elena (CS): FYI we've got a paying customer hit a weird rerank behavior. Their UI shows scores like [-0.3, 0.0, 4.5, 200] and their thresholding logic is completely broken. They expected probabilities (0-1).
Arjun (ML Eng): Thanks Elena. Those look like raw logits/score-head outputs (unbounded). Larger is better; negatives are normal. Do they require probabilities or just ordering?
Elena (CS): They insist on probabilities because they use >0.75 cutoff. They want simple guidance and a short pasteable snippet. They also asked if a huge value like 200 means something's gone wrong.
Sam (Backend): Two quick operational checks from infra: 1) confirm candidate count equals scores length, 2) check whether the request was batched or single-shot. We saw a past bug where batched responses were concatenated which created odd score ranges.
Elena (CS): Customer sent this minimal payload and response (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "rerank-v2",
  "api_version": "2026-01-15",
  "query": "cheap hotels near downtown",
  "candidates": ["c1","c2","c3","c4"]
}

response:
{
  "scores": [-0.3, 0.0, 4.5, 200]
}
```
Arjun (ML Eng): That definitely looks like logits. The absolute scale can vary by model and batch context; 200 is just a large positive logit. Recommend converting to probabilities client-side using softmax. Also warn about numerical stability when values are large.
Elena (CS): They asked for a one-sentence explanation for their product team: any concise phrasing?
Arjun (ML Eng): "Rerank returns raw model scores (logits). Higher is better. These are not probabilities; to get 0-1 probabilities over the returned candidates apply a softmax over the list of scores. If you need independent, non-mutually-exclusive probabilities, use a model that emits sigmoid-style scores per candidate."
Elena (CS): Perfect. Customer also asked for example code in JS and a note about numerical stability.
Arjun (ML Eng): Paste these snippets. Mention subtracting max before exponentiating.
JS example:
```js
const scores = [-0.3, 0.0, 4.5, 200];
const max = Math.max(...scores);
const exps = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s - max));
const sum = exps.reduce((a,b) => a + b, 0);
const probs = exps.map(e => e / sum);
console.log(probs);
// -> very close to [0, 0, 0, 1] because 200 dominates
```
Python example with stability note:
```py
scores = [-0.3, 0.0, 4.5, 200]
import math
mx = max(scores)
exp = [math.exp(s - mx) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
print(probs)
```
Sam (Backend): Confirmed in server logs we got a single request at 2026-03-14T15:12:22Z and the model run produced those scores. No reshapes or batching artifacts. last_message_ts=1802347915
Arjun (ML Eng): Also note: if your product relies on stable thresholds across models, logits won't work — scales shift by model variant. Options: 1) calibrate thresholds per-model and persist them, 2) use temperature scaling or isotonic regression with labeled eval set, or 3) ask us to expose a normalized option in API (feature request).
support-bot: Created internal ticket RED-2211 (docs + api-ux) assigned to Docs team.
Docs-bot: Suggested snippet added to internal drafts/rerank_guides.md (will publish after review).
Elena (CS): Customer accepted the explanation and snippets but asked: "Is there any case where negative score == invalid?"
Arjun (ML Eng): No. Negative logits just mean lower relative score. Only treat items as invalid if the API returns an explicit error or if the candidate count doesn't match scores.
Sam (Backend): Action items: 1) I'll add an e2e test to validate response shapes across rerank-v* and flag huge outliers (>1e6) as anomalous. ETA: 48h. 2) Elena will send the one-liner + JS + Python snippets to the customer. ETA: immediate.
Arjun (ML Eng): I'll pull together a short internal note describing calibration approaches (softmax, temperature, sigmoid for independent probs). ETA: 3 days.
Elena (CS): Closing the loop with customer now. They were satisfied with the explanation and will implement softmax conversion. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
